Nxeon hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`), single Proxmox host, real production system.

## Context

Off-site backups have been a known, flagged BLOCKER for this platform for a while (customer VM/data backups exist LOCALLY on this host, but nothing ships off-site — a real risk if this single host ever has a hardware failure). The owner wants automated offsite backups wired up to Mega (mega.io/mega.nz cloud storage) as the offsite destination.

## What already exists — read this first, don't rebuild it

`worker/backup-schedule.ts` and related backup code (`HostingBackup` model in `prisma/schema.prisma`, any `BACKUP_CREATE`/`BACKUP_RESTORE` job types in the `JobType` enum, `lib/game-control.ts`'s `readGameBackups`) — read all of this thoroughly to understand exactly how local backups currently work: what gets backed up (VM disk snapshots? file-level? both?), where they're stored on this host right now (check for a backup storage path/ZFS dataset — recall this host has a `tank/backup` ZFS pool, `df -h` showed `tank/backup 3.6T 183G 3.4T 6% /tank/backup`, that's very likely where local backups currently land), and how often/on what schedule.

## What to build

1. **Mega integration**: Mega doesn't have a simple REST API the way S3-compatible storage does — research the actual real options: `megacmd` (Mega's official CLI, installable via apt/their repo, supports scripted upload/sync — this is almost certainly the right approach for a server-side automated job, NOT a browser-based SDK), or their older `megatools` alternative. Pick whichever is the actually-correct, currently-maintained tool (check what's realistically installable on this Debian/Ubuntu host) rather than guessing.
2. **A new worker sweep** (or extend `worker/backup-schedule.ts` if it's the right place) that, on some schedule (daily is a reasonable default — check what the LOCAL backup schedule already is and either match it or run shortly after, so offsite always ships the freshest local backup), uploads/syncs new local backups from wherever they land (the ZFS backup pool, most likely) to a Mega account via the chosen CLI tool.
3. **Credentials**: Mega login credentials need to be provided by a human — you cannot create a Mega account or get real credentials yourself. Build the integration to read credentials from an env var or a `/etc/nxeon/*.env`-style file (matching the convention already used elsewhere in this codebase for third-party credentials — check `/etc/nxeon/` on this host for examples of the existing pattern) — e.g. `MEGA_EMAIL`/`MEGA_PASSWORD` or similar. Do NOT invent fake credentials or try to sign up for a real account yourself. If the tool needs credentials to even test basic connectivity, note clearly in your report that live end-to-end testing wasn't possible without them, and what you verified instead (the upload logic in isolation, dry-run mode if the CLI tool supports one, etc.).
4. **Admin visibility**: some way to see offsite-backup status in the admin portal (last successful offsite sync time, how many backups have shipped, any recent failures) — check `lib/admin-groups.ts` for where a backup-status nav item would sensibly live (probably under Fleet/Infrastructure) and follow the existing page/action conventions in this codebase.
5. **Retention**: don't just accumulate forever — a reasonable retention policy (e.g. keep the last N days offsite, matching or exceeding whatever the local retention already is) so Mega storage doesn't grow unbounded. Check Mega's real storage tier limits (mega.io/pricing) to inform a sensible default, but don't guess wildly — note your assumption clearly if you can't verify the account's actual plan/quota.

## Ground rules

- This is genuinely new infrastructure (a new scheduled job moving real backup data to a third-party service) — real caution warranted. Build and verify what you can WITHOUT real Mega credentials (the CLI tool install, the upload/sync logic, the admin UI, the retention logic as pure testable code where possible), and clearly flag exactly what still needs a human to do (get/provide Mega credentials, do one live end-to-end test) before this can actually run for real.
- `cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-offsitebackup -b feature/offsite-backup-mega`, symlink only `.env`, real `node_modules` via `npm ci`. Check `df -h /` first — if under 5GB free, stop and report. Delete your worktree's `node_modules`/`.next` once committed — hard requirement, a real disk-full production incident happened today from worktrees left with real node_modules copies.
- `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass clean. Add test coverage for any pure logic (retention-window calculation, etc.).
- Do NOT install anything system-wide on the live host outside your worktree without flagging it first in your report (e.g. if you need `apt install megacmd`, note that as a manual step for a human to approve/run, rather than just doing it — this touches the actual host, not just the app code). Commit your work but do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging/production, do NOT attempt to configure real Mega credentials or run a real upload.

Report back: what you found about the existing local backup system (what actually gets backed up, where, how often), which Mega CLI tool you chose and why, what you built, exactly what a human needs to do next (get Mega credentials, install the CLI on the host, provide the env vars, run one live test), the commit hash, and confirmation of disk cleanup.

=== backup-offsite.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Off-box backup replication.
#
# Copies the DB dumps, the host-configuration archives and (optionally) the
# whole-system VM archives to an OFFSITE target, so a chassis or disk loss does
# not take the backups with it.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHY THIS NOW FAILS INSTEAD OF EXITING 0
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This script used to `exit 0` when no target was configured, with a comment
# reading "not an error: intentionally inert until configured". The consequence,
# observed on this host: nxeon-backup-offsite.service ran at 04:20 on 2026-07-24,
# -07-25 and -07-26 and recorded `Result=success` every time, having copied
# nothing anywhere. systemd showed a green unit, the OnFailure=nxeon-alert@ hook
# never fired because nothing failed, and the admin portal had no page that would
# have said otherwise. For three days the platform reported working off-site
# backups while every byte it owned lived on one pool in one chassis.
#
# An inert backup that reports OK is worse than no backup at all: no backup at
# least leaves the operator's belief accurate. So an unconfigured target is now a
# hard failure — non-zero exit, systemd unit red, admin notification via
# nxeon-alert@ — and it stays red until someone actually configures a target or
# explicitly, deliberately acknowledges the risk.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THE OWNER MUST SET
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Edit /etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env and set exactly ONE of:
#
#   OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE="b2:nxeon-backups"
#       An rclone remote (Backblaze B2, S3, OVH/Hetzner object storage, …).
#       Requires: apt install rclone && rclone config — configure the remote as
#       ROOT, because this unit runs as root and reads root's
#       ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf.
#
#   OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET="user@host:/backups/nxeon"
#       rsync over SSH (rsync.net, a second box, a NAS). Requires key-based auth
#       for root with no passphrase prompt: ssh-keygen, ssh-copy-id, then verify
#       `ssh -o BatchMode=yes user@host true` succeeds as root.
#
# Optional:
#   OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1        also replicate the whole-system VM archives.
#                                Large (tens of GB/day) but this is the only copy
#                                that survives losing the chassis. Strongly
#                                recommended once bandwidth allows.
#   OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET=1      acknowledge "no off-site copy exists" and exit 0.
#                                ONLY for a deliberately single-chassis
#                                deployment. This is the switch that turns the
#                                alarm off; there is no other.
#
# SECURITY: the host-configuration archives contain /etc/pve/priv (cluster and CA
# private keys) and /etc/nxeon (Proxmox API token, Cloudflare token, mail
# credentials). Whatever target you choose therefore holds the keys to this
# platform. Use an rclone `crypt` remote, or a target you control with at-rest
# encryption — never a shared or public bucket.
#
# Exits non-zero on any real failure so the systemd OnFailure hook alerts admins.
set -uo pipefail

ENV_FILE="/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env"
SRC_DB="/tank/backup/db"
SRC_PLATFORM="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
STATUS="${STATUS_DIR}/offsite.json"

log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }

mkdir -p "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null && chmod 755 "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true

# The status file is what /admin/backups reads. The panel runs as the unprivileged
# `nxeon` user and cannot read /etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env (0600 root), so this
# is the only channel by which the portal can tell the owner the truth about
# off-site state — and it deliberately records the target KIND, never its value,
# so a bucket name or SSH host never leaks into a web page.
write_status() {
    local ok="$1" configured="$2" kind="$3" detail="$4"
    local last_success="null"
    # Preserve the previous successful-sync timestamp across a failing run, so the
    # panel can say "configured, but last succeeded 6 days ago" rather than losing
    # the only evidence that it ever worked.
    if [ "${ok}" = "true" ]; then
        last_success="\"$(date -Is)\""
    elif [ -f "${STATUS}" ]; then
        local prev
        prev="$(sed -n 's/.*"lastSuccessAt":\("[^"]*"\|null\).*/\1/p' "${STATUS}" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
        [ -n "${prev}" ] && last_success="${prev}"
    fi
    printf '{"ok":%s,"configured":%s,"kind":"%s","at":"%s","lastSuccessAt":%s,"detail":"%s"}\n' \
        "${ok}" "${configured}" "${kind}" "$(date -Is)" "${last_success}" "${detail}" > "${STATUS}"
    chmod 644 "${STATUS}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

[ -f "${ENV_FILE}" ] && . "${ENV_FILE}"

OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE="${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE:-}"
OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET="${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET:-}"
OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS="${OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS:-0}"
OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET="${OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET:-0}"

if [ -z "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}" ] && [ -z "${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET}" ]; then
    if [ "${OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET}" = "1" ]; then
        log "off-site replication DISABLED and acknowledged (OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET=1)"
        log "every backup this platform holds lives only on this chassis — accepted by the operator"
        write_status true false acknowledged "disabled and acknowledged by the operator"
        exit 0
    fi
    log "=============================================================="
    log "FAIL: OFF-SITE BACKUPS ARE NOT CONFIGURED"
    log "Every backup this platform holds — the customer database, the VM"
    log "archives, the /etc/pve definitions — exists on exactly ONE pool in"
    log "ONE chassis. Losing this box loses all of it, and that means losing"
    log "every customer's data with no recovery path."
    log ""
    log "Set exactly ONE of these in ${ENV_FILE}:"
    log "  OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE=\"b2:nxeon-backups\"        (apt install rclone; rclone config as root)"
    log "  OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET=\"user@host:/backups/nxeon\"  (root key-based SSH, BatchMode must work)"
    log ""
    log "Optional: OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1 to replicate the VM archives too."
    log "If this host is deliberately single-chassis, set OFFSITE_ACK_NO_TARGET=1"
    log "to acknowledge the risk and silence this failure. Do not silence it any"
    log "other way: this unit reporting success while copying nothing is exactly"
    log "the state it spent 2026-07-24..26 in."
    log "=============================================================="
    write_status false false none "no OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE or OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET set"
    exit 1
fi

if [ -n "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}" ] && [ -n "${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET}" ]; then
    log "FAIL: both OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE and OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET are set — pick exactly one"
    write_status false true ambiguous "both rclone and rsync targets are set"
    exit 1
fi

KIND="rsync"
[ -n "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}" ] && KIND="rclone"

if [ ! -d "${SRC_DB}" ]; then
    log "FAIL: ${SRC_DB} missing — there is nothing to replicate, which is itself the problem"
    write_status false true "${KIND}" "source ${SRC_DB} missing"
    exit 1
fi

# sync_one replicates one directory and then VERIFIES the target actually holds
# files. A transport that exits 0 without transferring anything (wrong remote
# path, silently empty source, an rclone remote pointing at a deleted bucket) is
# the same class of lie this script was rewritten to stop telling.
sync_one() {
    local src="$1" label="$2" rc=0
    local n_src
    n_src=$(find "${src}" -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name '*.partial' 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
    if [ "${n_src}" -eq 0 ]; then
        log "FAIL: ${label}: source ${src} holds no files — refusing to report a successful sync"
        return 1
    fi

    if [ "${KIND}" = "rclone" ]; then
        command -v rclone >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "FAIL: rclone not installed (apt install rclone)"; return 1; }
        log "rclone sync ${label}: ${src} (${n_src} file(s)) -> <remote>/${label}"
        rclone sync "${src}" "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}/${label}" \
            --transfers 4 --retries 3 --exclude '*.partial' || rc=$?
        [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || { log "FAIL: ${label} rclone exited ${rc}"; return 1; }
        # Post-sync assertion: the remote must now list files.
        local n_dst
        n_dst=$(rclone lsf "${OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE}/${label}" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
        if [ "${n_dst}" -eq 0 ]; then
            log "FAIL: ${label}: remote lists 0 files after a 'successful' sync"
            return 1
        fi
        log "OK ${label} replicated (${n_dst} file(s) present on the remote)"
    else
        command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "FAIL: rsync not installed"; return 1; }
        log "rsync ${label}: ${src} (${n_src} file(s)) -> <target>/${label}"
        rsync -az --delete --exclude '*.partial' \
            -e "ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ConnectTimeout=20" \
            "${src}/" "${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET}/${label}/" || rc=$?
        [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || { log "FAIL: ${label} rsync exited ${rc}"; return 1; }
        # Post-sync assertion: count files on the far side over the same transport.
        local host="${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET%%:*}" path="${OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET#*:}" n_dst
        n_dst=$(ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20 "${host}" \
            "find '${path}/${label}' -maxdepth 1 -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
        if [ "${n_dst}" -eq 0 ]; then
            log "FAIL: ${label}: target lists 0 files after a 'successful' sync"
            return 1
        fi
        log "OK ${label} replicated (${n_dst} file(s) present on the target)"
    fi
}

fail=0
synced=""

if sync_one "${SRC_DB}" "db"; then synced="${synced}db "; else fail=1; fi

# The host-configuration archives are ~50 KB and are the difference between
# "restore the VMs" and "rebuild every VM definition from memory". They are
# replicated unconditionally: there is no bandwidth argument against 50 KB.
# Staged into a temp dir so the VM archives in the same directory are not dragged
# along when OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS is off.
if [ -d "${SRC_PLATFORM}" ] && compgen -G "${SRC_PLATFORM}/host-config-*.tar.gz" >/dev/null; then
    if tmpdir="$(mktemp -d /tmp/nxeon-offsite-config.XXXXXX)"; then
        cp -p "${SRC_PLATFORM}"/host-config-*.tar.gz "${tmpdir}/" 2>/dev/null
        if sync_one "${tmpdir}" "host-config"; then synced="${synced}host-config "; else fail=1; fi
        rm -rf "${tmpdir}"
    else
        log "FAIL: could not stage host-config archives for replication"
        fail=1
    fi
else
    log "FAIL: no host-config-*.tar.gz in ${SRC_PLATFORM} — /etc/pve is not being captured."
    log "      Run scripts/backup-pve-config.sh (or the nxeon-backup-vms unit, which calls it)."
    fail=1
fi

if [ "${OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS}" = "1" ]; then
    if [ -d "${SRC_PLATFORM}" ]; then
        if sync_one "${SRC_PLATFORM}" "vms"; then synced="${synced}vms "; else fail=1; fi
    else
        log "FAIL: OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1 but ${SRC_PLATFORM} does not exist"
        fail=1
    fi
else
    log "note: OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS is not set — VM archives are NOT replicated off-site."
    log "      A chassis loss would still cost every VM image. Set OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1 when bandwidth allows."
fi

if [ "${fail}" -ne 0 ]; then
    write_status false true "${KIND}" "one or more replication targets failed"
    log "off-site replication FAILED"
    exit 1
fi

write_status true true "${KIND}" "replicated: ${synced% }"
log "off-site replication complete (${synced% })"

# Megarc Configuration File Format

**File Format (INI-style):**
The configuration uses section headers in brackets with key-value pairs. Per the documentation: `"[Username]"`, `"[Password]"`, `"[Network]"`, `"[Cache]"`, `"[Upload]"`, and `"[UI]"` sections are available, with all names being case-sensitive.

**Default Locations:**
Configuration files are read from `~/.megarc` or `./.megarc` (current directory or user home directory).

**Specifying Custom Config Path:**
According to the manual, `"explicit path to the config file was given via --config <path>"` allows you to override the default locations.

**Example Structure:**
```
[Login]
Username = your@email
Password = yourpassword
[Network]
SpeedLimit = 1024
Proxy = socks5://127.0.0.1:9050
ParallelTransfers = 2
[UI]
Colors = true
```

**Password Escaping Note:**
`"If you have back slash in your password, you must escape it with another backslash."` For instance, a password containing backslashes requires doubling them in the config file.

# Megacopy Options Summary

## Full Options List

**Authentication:**
- `-u <email>, --username <email>` — Account username
- `-p <password>, --password <password>` — Account password
- `--no-ask-password` — Never prompt for password interactively
- `--config <path>` — Load configuration from file
- `--ignore-config-file` — Disable loading .megarc

**Core Operations:**
- `-r <remotepath>, --remote <remotepath>` — Remote directory path
- `-l <path>, --local <path>` — Local directory path
- `-d, --download` — Download from Mega.nz (default is upload)
- `-n, --dryrun` — Preview changes without executing them

**Transfer Control:**
- `--no-progress` — Disable progress reporting
- `--limit-speed <speed>` — Set max upload/download speed in KiB/s
- `--disable-resume` — Don't resume partial downloads
- `--enable-previews` / `--disable-previews` — Control file preview generation
- `--proxy <proxy>` — Use proxy server

**Other:**
- `--reload` — Refresh filesystem cache
- `--debug [<options>]` — Enable debugging
- `--version` — Display version info

Yes, `-n` is confirmed as a genuine dry-run flag: "Don't perform any actual changes, just print what would be done."

## File Deletion Policy

The tool explicitly states: "No files are ever overwritten or removed." It only uploads new files—it never deletes remote files lacking local counterparts and never overwrites existing files.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Nxeon — host configuration backup (the bare-metal rebuild set).
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS: nothing on this box backed up /etc/pve. The VM *disks* were
# being dumped by vzdump, but /etc/pve/qemu-server/<vmid>.conf — the file that
# says how much RAM a guest has, which bridge and MAC its NIC uses, which disks
# it owns and in what order, plus /etc/pve/storage.cfg, /etc/pve/user.cfg and the
# firewall rules — existed in exactly one place: this chassis. After a total host
# loss you would have had a directory full of vzdump archives and no VM
# definitions to restore them into, no storage named `vmdata` for them to land
# on, and no record of the network layout. `qmrestore` reads the config out of
# the archive for the guest itself, but the *host* side (storage.cfg, bridges,
# users, ACLs, the Nxeon systemd units) would have had to be reconstructed from
# memory. This script is small, fast (~16 KB of config) and runs before the
# multi-gigabyte guest dumps so the cheapest, most irreplaceable data is
# captured first.
#
# Also snapshots the *interpretation* of that config (pvesm status, pveversion,
# zpool status, ip addr) as plain text, because a rebuild is done by a human
# reading it, not only by a machine restoring it.
#
# Idempotent / re-runnable. Deletes nothing except its own aged-out archives.
set -uo pipefail

DEST_DIR="${NXEON_PLATFORM_BACKUP_DIR:-/tank/backup/platform}"
STATUS_DIR="${NXEON_BACKUP_STATUS_DIR:-/tank/backup/status}"
KEEP_LAST="${NXEON_CONFIG_BACKUP_KEEP:-3}"
TS="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
DEST="${DEST_DIR}/host-config-${TS}.tar.gz"

log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; }

mkdir -p "${DEST_DIR}" "${STATUS_DIR}" || { log "FAIL: cannot create ${DEST_DIR}"; exit 1; }
chmod 755 "${DEST_DIR}" "${STATUS_DIR}" 2>/dev/null || true

if [ ! -d /etc/pve ]; then
    log "FAIL: /etc/pve does not exist — is this a Proxmox host?"
    exit 1
fi

# Plain-text state snapshots, gathered into the archive alongside the raw config.
# A rebuilder needs to know what the pools/versions/interfaces *were*, and none of
# that is recoverable from /etc/pve alone.
work="$(mktemp -d /tmp/nxeon-config-backup.XXXXXX)" || { log "FAIL: mktemp"; exit 1; }
trap 'rm -rf "${work}"' EXIT
snap="${work}/state"
mkdir -p "${snap}"

{
    echo "# Nxeon host state snapshot — ${TS}"
    echo "# hostname: $(hostname -f 2>/dev/null || hostname)"
} > "${snap}/README.txt"

pveversion -v            >"${snap}/pveversion.txt"      2>&1 || true
pvesm status             >"${snap}/pvesm-status.txt"    2>&1 || true
qm list                  >"${snap}/qm-list.txt"         2>&1 || true
zpool status             >"${snap}/zpool-status.txt"    2>&1 || true
zfs list -o name,used,avail,mountpoint >"${snap}/zfs-list.txt" 2>&1 || true
ip -o addr               >"${snap}/ip-addr.txt"         2>&1 || true
ip route                 >"${snap}/ip-route.txt"        2>&1 || true

2	# Off-box backup replication.
3	#
4	# Copies the DB dumps, the host-configuration archives and (optionally) the
5	# whole-system VM archives to an OFFSITE target, so a chassis or disk loss does
6	# not take the backups with it.
7	#
8	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
9	# WHY THIS NOW FAILS INSTEAD OF EXITING 0
10	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
11	# This script used to `exit 0` when no target was configured, with a comment
12	# reading "not an error: intentionally inert until configured". The consequence,
13	# observed on this host: nxeon-backup-offsite.service ran at 04:20 on 2026-07-24,
14	# -07-25 and -07-26 and recorded `Result=success` every time, having copied
15	# nothing anywhere. systemd showed a green unit, the OnFailure=nxeon-alert@ hook
16	# never fired because nothing failed, and the admin portal had no page that would
17	# have said otherwise. For three days the platform reported working off-site
18	# backups while every byte it owned lived on one pool in one chassis.
19	#
20	# An inert backup that reports OK is worse than no backup at all: no backup at
21	# least leaves the operator's belief accurate. So an unconfigured target is now a
22	# hard failure — non-zero exit, systemd unit red, admin notification via
23	# nxeon-alert@ — and it stays red until someone actually configures a target or
24	# explicitly, deliberately acknowledges the risk.
25	#
26	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
27	# WHAT THE OWNER MUST SET
28	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29	# Edit /etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env and set exactly ONE of:

31	#   OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE="b2:nxeon-backups"

33	#       Requires: apt install rclone && rclone config — configure the remote as

35	#       ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf.

## Summary

**What already existed (and I didn't rebuild):** The offsite backup blocker turned out to already have a substantial, hardened implementation on the host that isn't mentioned anywhere in the repo's obvious backup files — I found it by checking `/etc/nxeon/` and `systemctl list-timers`:

- `scripts/backup-offsite.sh` + `nxeon-backup-offsite.timer` (daily 04:20) — a bash/systemd pipeline that already replicates `/tank/backup/db` (Postgres dumps, 14-day local retention), `/tank/backup/platform` host-config archives (`/etc/pve`, keep-last 3), and optionally VM disk archives, to an `rclone` remote or `rsync` target.
- It's deliberately **fail-loud**: an incident on 2026-07-24..26 (documented in the script's own header) had it silently reporting success while shipping nothing; it now hard-fails until a target is configured or explicitly acknowledged.
- `/admin/backups` already renders offsite status live via `lib/platform-backups.ts` reading `/tank/backup/status/offsite.json` — admin visibility (task item 4) was already built, generically, for any target kind.
- Local retention already exists per-subsystem (db: 14 days age-pruned; VM/host-config: keep-last-3), enforced by `scripts/backup-db.sh` / `backup-vms.sh` / `backup-pve-config.sh`.

Given this, I extended that existing pipeline with Mega as a third target rather than building a parallel Node/worker system — `worker/backup-schedule.ts`, `HostingBackup`, `BACKUP_CREATE`/`BACKUP_RESTORE` jobs, and `lib/game-control.ts::readGameBackups` are all customer/per-VM backup mechanisms, unrelated to this platform-level DR pool, and I left them untouched.

**Tool choice: `megatools`, not `megacmd`.** `megacmd` is Mega's official, more actively maintained CLI, but it isn't in this host's apt mirror and requires adding Mega's own repo (unverified for Debian trixie). `megatools` (`megacopy`/`megals`/`megamkdir`/`megarm`) resolves directly from the already-configured mirror (`apt-cache policy megatools` → candidate 1.11.5-1) with no new repo, and its `megacopy` command has exactly the primitives needed: `-n` dry-run, `--local`/`--remote` directory mirroring, `--config` for credential-file auth (avoiding password-in-`ps`).

**What I built** (worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-offsitebackup`, branch `feature/offsite-backup-mega`, commit `7e4675c`):
- `scripts/backup-offsite.sh`: added `mega` as a third `KIND`, gated on `OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE` + `MEGA_EMAIL`/`MEGA_PASSWORD` in `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env`. Writes credentials to a `mktemp`'d 0600 `--config` file per run, shredded on exit via trap — never passed as CLI args. Supports `OFFSITE_MEGA_DRYRUN=1` for safe first testing. Same post-sync existence assertion discipline as the rclone/rsync paths.
- Since `megacopy` is upload-only by design (never deletes), added an explicit prune step: `lib/offsite-retention.ts` (pure, unit-tested — mirror rule + an age-cap backstop) and `scripts/mega-prune-plan.ts` (thin CLI the bash script pipes `megals` output through). Only the mirror rule (delete remote files no longer present locally) is wired live — it needs just filenames, which `megals` gives reliably. The age-cap rule is implemented/tested but not wired to `megals -l` timestamps, since I couldn't verify that output format against a live account.
- `lib/platform-backups.ts`: surfaces the per-run prune count in the existing `/admin/backups` offsite panel — no new page needed.
- `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env`: added the (fully commented-out, inert) Mega option block, matching the existing rclone/rsync documentation pattern in that same file.
- 8 new unit tests, all passing; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run build` succeeds; full suite shows the same 33 pre-existing failures as `main` (unrelated to this change — verified by diffing test counts against `main`).

**What a human must still do before this runs for real:**
1. Get a Mega account and credentials (I did not sign up for one).
2. `apt install megatools` on the host (not done — flagging per instructions, since it touches the live host).
3. Set `OFFSITE_MEGA_REMOTE`, `MEGA_EMAIL`, `MEGA_PASSWORD` in `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env`.
4. Run once with `OFFSITE_MEGA_DRYRUN=1`, confirm the plan looks right, then run for real: `systemctl start nxeon-backup-offsite`.
5. **Timing bug I found (not caused by my change, pre-existing):** the offsite timer fires at 04:20, but `nxeon-backup-vms.timer` (which also writes the host-config archive) fires at 04:30 — so whenever `OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1`, offsite systematically ships yesterday's VM/host-config archives, one day stale. I did not touch the live `.timer` file (it's host config, not tracked in git, outside my worktree) — recommend moving `nxeon-backup-offsite.timer`'s `OnCalendar` to something safely after 04:30 plus VM-dump headroom (e.g. `06:00`), given `nxeon-backup-vms.service` has a 6h `TimeoutStartSec`.
6. Retention default is 30 days, chosen to match the local PREMIUM tier's "keep a month" precedent — flagged as an assumption in `lib/offsite-retention.ts` since I couldn't verify the actual Mega account's plan/quota.

**Cleanup confirmed:** `node_modules` (1.1G) and `.next` (1.4G) deleted from the worktree after committing; `df -h /` is back to 22G free (started at 19G free, same ballpark as before I began). Not merged to main; nothing on staging/production touched except the inert env-file comment block.
